what_its_for: Ciclesonide is a steroid (corticosteroid) medicine that helps reduce swelling and irritation in your airways or nose. It is used to prevent and control asthma symptoms (Alvesco inhaler) and to relieve stuffy, runny, or itchy nose caused by allergies (Omnaris and Zetonna nasal sprays). It does NOT work right away during a sudden asthma attack — it is a controller medicine you use every day.
how_to_take: FOR THE INHALER (Alvesco): Shake gently if instructed, then breathe out fully away from the inhaler. Place the mouthpiece in your mouth, seal your lips around it, and breathe in slowly and deeply as you press down on the canister. Hold your breath for about 10 seconds, then breathe out slowly. Rinse your mouth with water and spit it out after each use — do NOT swallow the water. This helps prevent a mouth or throat infection (thrush). FOR THE NASAL SPRAY (Omnaris or Zetonna): Blow your nose gently before using. Shake the bottle if directed. Tilt your head slightly forward. Insert the nozzle into one nostril pointing slightly away from the center of your nose. Press down to spray while breathing in gently through your nose. Breathe out through your mouth. Repeat for the other nostril. Avoid blowing your nose for at least a few minutes after use. Prime the spray before the first use or if unused for several days — point it away from you and spray into the air until a fine mist appears.
dosing: ASTHMA INHALER (Alvesco): Adults and teenagers (12 years and older): Usually 80 mcg to 320 mcg once or twice daily depending on how severe your asthma is. Your doctor will set the right dose for you. Do not use more than prescribed. NASAL SPRAY for Allergies (Omnaris): Adults and children 6 years and older: Usually 2 sprays in each nostril once a day (200 mcg total per day). (Zetonna): Adults and children 12 years and older: Usually 1 spray in each nostril once a day. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's exact instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time or double up to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, open flames, and direct sunlight. Do NOT puncture or throw the inhaler canister into a fire even when it seems empty. Keep the cap on the nasal spray when not in use. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not store in the bathroom where it can get damp.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting the spray or inhaler medicine in your eyes. Do not stop using ciclesonide suddenly without talking to your doctor first, especially if you have been using it for a long time. Avoid exposing yourself to chickenpox or measles if you have never had them or been vaccinated — steroid medicines can make infections harder to fight. Do not use the nasal spray if your nose is blocked completely; use a decongestant first as directed by your doctor. Avoid smoking, as it can make your breathing condition worse.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you have: a sudden worsening of breathing or wheezing; white patches or sores in your mouth or throat (possible thrush/yeast infection); vision changes or eye pain; signs of a serious infection such as fever, chills, or feeling very unwell; unusual weakness or tiredness; nosebleeds that do not stop or a hole in the wall between your nostrils (nasal septum); signs of a severe allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; or if your asthma symptoms are not improving or getting worse after a few weeks of use.
when_it_works: Ciclesonide is NOT a rescue medicine — it will NOT relieve a sudden asthma attack or immediate allergy symptoms. For asthma control, you may start to notice improvement within 1 to 2 weeks, but it can take up to 4 to 8 weeks to get the full benefit. For nasal allergy symptoms, some people feel better within 1 to 2 days, but full improvement may take 1 to 2 weeks. Keep using it every day as prescribed even if you feel well.
special_populations: CHILDREN: The nasal spray (Omnaris) can be used in children 6 years and older. The inhaler (Alvesco) is for ages 12 and older. Long-term use of steroids in children may slow growth — your child's doctor will monitor their height regularly. PREGNANCY AND BREASTFEEDING: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Uncontrolled asthma during pregnancy can be harmful, so your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks. OLDER ADULTS: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as bone thinning (osteoporosis). Talk to your doctor about calcium and vitamin D supplements and bone health monitoring. IMMUNE SYSTEM PROBLEMS: If your immune system is weakened due to a disease or medicine, tell your doctor before using ciclesonide.
